scope.role: Supplement only. Does not replace or rewrite the saved full original payload.

massWeightGuard.disposition: Refresh of the bounded native guard only. The previous hash is historical and must not be restored.

comparisons.testedFact: For one photon E=hν, so doubling frequency doubles photon energy.
comparisons.comparison: The threshold neighbor asks whether a below-threshold light beam emits electrons when intensity rises; the work-function neighbor asks the minimum energy to remove an electron; the photoelectric-effect neighbor names electron emission. This card tests proportional photon energy, without asserting threshold behavior.

comparisons.testedFact: Escape speed is the minimum initial speed to reach infinity with zero residual speed; in the ideal surface model v=sqrt(2gR).
comparisons.comparison: The gravity-direction neighbor asks for the direction of local gravitational acceleration. This card computes an energy threshold speed from g and R; it tests magnitude and energy balance, not force direction.

comparisons.testedFact: A pressure change in enclosed fluid is transmitted; equal pressure across piston areas yields F1/A1=F2/A2 and allows the output-force calculation.
comparisons.comparison: The pressure-force-area neighbor defines pressure as force per area. The Pascal card uses that relationship across two pistons with a supplied area ratio to calculate output force; it does not merely ask for the definition. Bernoulli concerns the energy relation in flowing fluid and is not invoked.

comparisons.testedFact: An approaching source compresses forward wavefront spacing; the stationary observer receives wavefronts more often and hears higher frequency.
comparisons.comparison: The neighbor asks for the name of the general source/observer-motion phenomenon. This card asks for the directional prediction and physical wavefront cause in one specified approach case. It does not ask for the general definition or the receding-source inverse case.

comparisons.testedFact: After two half-life intervals, expected remaining fraction is 1/2 × 1/2 = 1/4.
comparisons.comparison: The neighbor defines the duration that halves the undecayed population once. This card applies the definition over two intervals, testing repeated halving rather than term recall.

comparisons.testedFact: For an isolated system total entropy does not decrease; it is constant for a reversible process and increases for an irreversible one.
comparisons.comparison: The entropy-disorder neighbor describes entropy via microstate distribution and only briefly mentions nondecrease. This card directly asks for the second-law condition on an isolated system. The heat-direction neighbor concerns spontaneous transfer from hot to cold, a related consequence but a different predicate; neither is posed as the inverse.

comparisons.testedFact: Changing magnetic flux induces EMF even in an open circuit; current requires a closed conducting path.
comparisons.comparison: The induction-current-field neighbor names the induction/flux relation; this card asks whether EMF exists when the switch is open and distinguishes it from current. The pair is adjacent and deliberately complementary: flux change is sufficient for EMF, while an open path blocks current. Lenz's-law direction and magnetic-flux definition answer different questions. The distractor claiming no EMF in an open circuit is explicitly rejected by the source.

comparisons.testedFact: Total internal reflection requires travel from higher to lower refractive index and incidence angle greater than the critical angle.
comparisons.comparison: The critical-angle neighbor asks for the boundary-angle term; refraction-medium and refractive-index neighbors define separate optical concepts. This card combines both necessary conditions in a glass-to-air case; it does not claim that either condition alone is sufficient.

comparisons.testedFact: Convert Celsius to kelvins with T(K)=t(°C)+273.15; distance above absolute zero is the resulting kelvin value.
comparisons.comparison: The water cards test phase-change reference temperatures, while temperature-warmth is a general definition. This item applies the Celsius/Kelvin offset near the absolute-zero reference; it does not confuse 0 °C with 0 K.

comparisons.testedFact: In a closed system, total linear momentum before and after a perfectly inelastic collision is equal; divide by combined mass to get the shared speed.
comparisons.comparison: The momentum-mass-velocity neighbor defines p=mv, which is an input relation used here rather than the answer. The target applies system conservation to two bodies that stick together. Impulse-force-time concerns momentum change from force over time; angular momentum is a different rotational quantity.
